note: Every rule below carries a legal/regulatory source. This file is read by the rule engine at runtime; it is not hardcoded in application code. Update last_verified whenever a rule is re-checked against source. Thresholds a nodal ministry/tender can override must be re-read from the tender config, not this file, when tender_override_allowed is true.

rules.source: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 — Section 25 (registration)

rules.requirement: GST registration threshold applicability (informational — not a bid-blocking rule by itself)
rules.source: CGST Act, 2017 — Section 22; threshold notifications by CBIC (varies by state/category, goods vs services)
rules.condition: N/A — informational only, verify against current CBIC notification before enforcing as a hard rule
rules.warning: GST registration threshold varies by state and by goods/services category and has changed via notification multiple times. Do not hardcode a number here — flag for officer review if bidder claims threshold-exemption.

rules.source: MSMED Act, 2006; Udyam Registration Notification (26 June 2020, as amended)

rules.requirement: MSME classification (micro / small / medium) meets tender's required tier(s), where the tender restricts eligibility by MSME tier
rules.source: MSME Classification Gazette Notification, 21 March 2025 (Ministry of MSME) — revised investment and turnover ceilings; Union Budget 2025-26 revision
rules.notes: Both investment AND turnover must independently fall within the tier ceiling; if either exceeds the ceiling, enterprise moves to the next tier. Export turnover is excluded from the turnover calculation per the same notification. Udyam auto-populates turnover from IT/GSTN records rather than self-declaration. tender.required_msme_tier is a list, e.g. ['micro','small'] for an MSE-reserved tender — classification alone is not a verdict without this.

rules.requirement: Bidder identity must remain consistent across PAN, GST and Udyam records
rules.source: General procurement due-diligence principle; not a single statutory citation — cross-document consistency is a compliance-verification best practice referenced across GeM bidder-eligibility guidance
normalization_rules: normalize common legal suffixes (Pvt Ltd / Private Limited / P. Ltd / LLP, etc.)
rules.notes: CONFLICT must never auto-reject. Route to manual review — a mismatch can have a legitimate explanation (trade name vs legal name, recent name change not yet updated across registries, etc).

rules.requirement: Minimum annual turnover as specified by tender
rules.source: Tender-specific eligibility clause (General Financial Rules, 2017, Rule 173 — financial capacity criteria are set per-tender by the procuring entity, not a fixed statutory number)
rules.notes: This threshold MUST be read from the specific tender's requirement config, never from this file. This entry only documents the rule's evaluation logic.

rules.requirement: Local content classification meets tender's required class for Make in India preference
rules.source: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017, as amended by DPIIT
rules.notes: Default thresholds are 50% (Class-I) and 20% (Class-II) per the 2017 Order, but the nodal ministry/department can notify a higher or lower minimum for a specific item category — read tender.required_local_content_class from the tender config, never assume a default here. For bids below Rs 200 crore, only Class-I and Class-II local suppliers are eligible to bid at all; a non-local classification below that threshold is a genuine ineligibility, not an exemption.

rules.requirement: OEM authorization letter present (when bidder is not the manufacturer)
rules.source: Tender-specific eligibility clause; standard GeM bid-document requirement for reseller/dealer bids
rules.condition: authorization.present == true AND authorization.oem_name matches tender.required_oem (if specified)
rules.notes: NOT_APPLICABLE when the bidder is itself the OEM/manufacturer — do not evaluate as VIOLATION in that case.

rules.requirement: MSE purchase preference eligibility (informational, not a bid-blocking rule)
rules.source: Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (PPP-MSE) Order, 2012, amended 2018 — Section 11, MSMED Act, 2006
rules.condition: N/A — this determines preference/reservation eligibility (25% MSE procurement target, 4% SC/ST-owned sub-target, 3% women-owned sub-target, L1+15% purchase preference), not pass/fail compliance
rules.notes: Surface this as informational context in the officer dashboard, not as a compliance verdict.

rules.requirement: EPFO registration (when tender requires labour-law compliance evidence and bidder headcount is disclosed)
rules.source: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 — Section 1(3)
rules.notes: 'Once covered, always covered' — an establishment that crossed 20 employees remains covered even if headcount later drops. Only evaluate if the tender explicitly requires labour-compliance evidence; do not apply to every tender by default.

rules.requirement: ESIC registration (when tender requires labour-law compliance evidence and bidder headcount is disclosed)
rules.source: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, as amended; Code on Social Security, 2020 (ESI provisions effective November 2025)
rules.notes: Threshold is 10 employees in most major states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, etc.); 20 in a small number of states/UTs. Default to 10 unless tender specifies bidder's state and that state's notified threshold is known to be 20.

rules.source: General Financial Rules, 2017 — Rule 151 (banning of business dealings); CVC/Ministry debarment orders
rules.notes: This is a CRITICAL rule (see critical_override_rule_ids below): a VIOLATION here must force risk_level = HIGH and manual_review = true regardless of the overall numeric score, per the score/risk critical-rule-override principle.

scoring.formula: score = round(100 * sum(weight for each evaluated requirement) / count(requirements where verdict != NOT_APPLICABLE))

risk_bands.MEDIUM: score >= 60 AND score < 85 AND no critical_override triggered
risk_bands.HIGH: score < 60 OR any critical_override rule fired
